CakePHP and Slim apps to PHP 8.5#

This page covers the three framework hops for CakePHP and Slim apps: the commands, what each hop changes, and the MANUAL list each one prints. Before this: Hand-copied libraries to Composer. Next: CakePHP and Slim apps onto Laravel.

Booster 1.20 takes a CakePHP 4 app to CakePHP 5.4 and a Slim 3 app to Slim 4.15, and moves PHP to 8.5 around those steps. The frameworks hold PHP back: CakePHP 4.5 stops at PHP 8.3 and Slim 3.12 at 7.3, so the PHP hops wait for the framework hop that lets them go on. PHP 8.6 is out; Booster's 8.6 hops follow once CakePHP and Slim support it.

CakePHP and Slim are being phased out at WSU (D-124): these hops keep existing apps supported; new apps start on raw PHP or Laravel (Sourdough or WELD).

composer global require waynestate/booster:^1.20
booster detect --path=../my-app
booster plan   --path=../my-app --to-php 8.5
booster run    --path=../my-app --replay --to-php 8.5

detect names the framework and its major.minor (framework cakephp 4.5 or framework slim 3.12), read from composer.lock. With no lock, detect shows the floor of the composer.json constraint, but plan uses the line Composer would install: the newest line that constraint allows on the app's PHP (slim/slim ^4.10 plans as Slim 4.15). plan puts the framework hops between the PHP hops, and run applies them one at a time, each gated by the app's tests and the replay. Pass --to-php 8.5 to both: it keeps the plan and the run on the same target. --to-cakephp and --to-slim pick the framework line (the newest by default; --to-cakephp 4 stops on 4.6).

Point Booster at the folder with composer.json. Plenty of Slim apps keep it under src/, next to the code, not at the repository root. Booster reads the framework from that file and refuses a hop without it, so give it that folder:

booster plan --path=../my-app/src --to-php 8.5

--replay matters here. The tests a CakePHP or Slim app ships with (often the skeleton's, or none) prove very little about a framework move, so the replay is the real gate for both frameworks. Run booster replay init --path=../my-app first and read the draft (see The replay gate). For Slim it lists the route calls it finds with their group prefixes, including groups that call a class's static addRoutes($app) in another file; keep at least one request per group, which is what catches a group that lost its prefix. For CakePHP it serves webroot/index.php, creates the tmp/ and logs/ folders git does not keep, sets DEBUG=false and a fake salt, and drafts the routes in config/routes.php (scopes, prefixes, connect() and the verb routes, one request per page template for /pages/*) plus, where the file calls fallbacks(), one request per public controller action. Check the draft against bin/cake routes, fill in the ids, and delete the actions that change data.

What a CakePHP 4 app gets#

Two hops, cakephp-4-to-4.6 then cakephp-4.6-to-5, with the PHP hops between them:

  1. cakephp-4-to-4.6 runs CakePHP's own upgrade rules for 4.1 through 4.5 (cakephp/upgrade, in a container, over a copy of the app, so a rule set that fails halfway leaves the app as it was), then requires cakephp/cakephp ^4.6 and the matching versions of the CakePHP plugins the app already lists. It goes first, on the PHP the app runs today, when that is 7.4 or newer; an app below 7.4 gets the PHP hops to 7.4 first, then this one.
  2. PHP moves to 8.2, the first PHP CakePHP 5.4 runs on.
  3. cakephp-4.6-to-5 runs the 5.0 through 5.4 rules (with Chronos 3 and Migrations), renames .ctp templates to .php under templates/ and moves the locales, moves AuthComponent to the Authentication plugin, swaps the Oracle driver if the app has it, and requires CakePHP 5.4 with the plugins that match.
  4. PHP moves on to 8.5.

A CakePHP 4.3 app on PHP 8.1 therefore plans cakephp-4-to-4.6, php-81-to-82, cakephp-4.6-to-5, then php-82-to-83, php-83-to-84 and php-84-to-85. The same app on PHP 7.3 plans php-73-to-74 first, then cakephp-4-to-4.6, then the same course. Stop on 4.6 with --to-cakephp 4: it still runs on PHP 8.5, but 4.x is end of life, so treat it as a rest stop, not a home. A target PHP below 8.2 leaves the CakePHP 5 step out with a warning, --skip cakephp-4.6-to-5 leaves it out too, and the PHP hops then stay within what 4.6 runs on.

Install first for a dry run. The rules read the app's own vendor/ (mounted read-only), so run composer install in the app before a --dry-run; a real run's baseline does it for you.

Fix deprecations first. Run your tests with error_reporting(E_ALL) on CakePHP 4.6 and fix every deprecation notice before the 5 step. A deprecation on 4.6 is CakePHP 5 knocking politely; on 5 it stops knocking. Booster tells you; it does not fix them for you.

The sign-in move. The 5 step moves the like-for-like AuthComponent calls ($this->Auth->user('x') reads the identity, setUser() becomes setIdentity(), logout() keeps its name on $this->Authentication, allow() becomes addUnauthenticatedActions()), swaps loadComponent('Auth') for loadComponent('Authentication.Authentication'), requires cakephp/authentication ^3.0, and wires src/Application.php: the provider interface, the plugin, the middleware (after CSRF protection, else body parsing, else routing: AuthComponent checked inside the controller, so inside every middleware), and a service with the Session authenticator whose guests go to the old loginAction. AuthComponent never asked for a sign-in on its own loginAction; the plugin does, so the page would redirect to itself. Booster names that action in addUnauthenticatedActions() at the end of its controller's initialize() (or adds an initialize()), and says MANUAL when the loginAction is not a plain controller and action array.

The guests' redirect stays AuthComponent's, so the replay sees the same answer: the service's getUnauthenticatedRedirectUrl() sends a full URL (Router::url($loginAction, true)), adds ?redirect= with the page the guest asked for except the home page, and flashes the app's authError first (AuthComponent's default message when the app set none, nothing for false), with AuthComponent's flash options. The plugin alone would send a path, always add the way back, and flash nothing.

The skeleton's own files. The 5 step also makes the CakePHP 5 skeleton's moves no upgrade rule makes: config/bootstrap.php loads CakePHP's global functions (require CAKE . 'functions.php';, without which env() is undefined), phpunit.xml loads the fixture extension the PHPUnit 10 way and names the covered code in <source>, loadComponent('RequestHandler') goes when nothing reads the component (with a viewClasses() for JSON and XML on AppController when config/routes.php sets those extensions), log 'scopes' => false becomes null, the core cache follows its _cake_translations_ rename, and a template's Connection::connect() goes through the driver.

PHPUnit waits for CakePHP 5. CakePHP 4's TestCase does not load on PHPUnit 10, so a CakePHP 4 app on PHPUnit 9 keeps it until the 5 step, which requires PHPUnit 11.5 with CakePHP 5.4; the PHPUnit 12 and 13 hops follow. A run that PHPUnit 12 fails only for the skeleton's <ini name="apc.enable_cli"> (the gate image has no APCu) passes with a note, every test green. The replay switches on the cakephp normalizer from the 5 step, which hides only the extra rel="shortcut icon" link CakePHP 4's meta('icon') printed.

What Booster does not do (the MANUAL list). Each run prints these as MANUAL: lines, with the file and the count where there is one. The scan reads code, not // or /* */ comments, so code the app commented out is not a step; doc blocks still count (an @property that names AuthComponent is a stale type to update):

  • On the 4.6 step: the reminder to fix every deprecation with E_ALL before the 5 step.
  • On the 4.6 step: the Cake\Network\Socket properties CakePHP 4.3 turned into methods (connected is isConnected(), encrypted is isEncrypted(), lastError is lastError()). The upstream rule for them needs a Rector class that no longer exists, so Booster leaves them to you; search your code for them.
  • On both steps: View::loadHelper() calls the rules could not type (it is addHelper() since 4.5).
  • Sign-in that is not a plain session: isAuthorized() (move it to Authorization plugin policies or plain controller code), and any Auth config the plugin has no like-for-like for (authenticate with a custom authenticator such as CAS, an SSO cookie or an LTI launch, authorize, loginRedirect, logoutRedirect; loginAction and authError are carried over into the guests' redirect). An authError that is not a string or a __() call on strings (Booster flashes no message then), and a custom flash config (Booster uses AuthComponent's default flash options). Also an 'Auth' entry with config in a $components list, any other $this->Auth->...() call, what the action does with logout()'s return value (now the redirect URL or null), and allow() calls that passed a variable (it could hold one name or null, every action). allow() added to the actions guests may reach, so it becomes addUnauthenticatedActions(), never allowUnauthenticated(), which replaces the list; one name goes in an array, and allow() with nothing is disableIdentityCheck().
  • src/Application.php that Booster could not wire: no such file or class, one that already provides an authentication service (check that it loads the Session authenticator), no bootstrap() or middleware(), no routing middleware, or no loginAction found (the redirect is the placeholder /login).
  • Code no rule moves: RequestHandlerComponent where the app still reads $this->RequestHandler (declare viewClasses() instead), a check that the controllers that serialize still answer .json and .xml after Booster added viewClasses(), ->withType() calls, Cake\Mailer\Email (use Mailer), Cake\I18n\Time and the mutable Cake\I18n\Date (use DateTime or the immutable Date, and check code that changed a date in place), and any .ctp template left over.
  • cakedc/cakephp-oracle-driver has no CakePHP 5 release. The 5 step swaps it for ioigoume/cakephp5-oracle-driver and renames its namespace; check that it covers the Oracle calls your app makes.
  • App bugs the move exposes are reported, never fixed: the hop moves the framework, not the app's own logic.

What a Slim 3 app gets#

One hop, slim-3-to-4, at the lowest PHP Slim 4.15 runs on (7.4: first when the app is already there, else right after the PHP hop that lands on 7.4), then the PHP hops to 8.5. --to-slim 3.13 is refused: Booster moves Slim 3 apps to Slim 4.15.

  • new \Slim\App([...]) becomes LegacyApp::create([...]) over your existing Pimple container, which keeps every $container['x'], $c->x and $c->get('x') working, and LegacyApp::finish($app) goes in just before $app->run(). No PHP-DI rewrite. The five glue files (LegacyContainer, LegacyDoublePass, LegacyApp, LegacyEnvironment, LegacyHttp) are written into a Legacy folder under the app's PSR-4 root, so they are your code from then on. An app with no PSR-4 autoload entry (the official Slim 3 skeleton has only autoload-dev) gets a stop sign from plan, and the hop refuses it: add one ("autoload": {"psr-4": {"App\\": "src/"}}), run composer dump-autoload and commit first.
  • The container keeps Slim 3's own entries: environment, request and response exist when the app did not set them, and the notFoundHandler, notAllowedHandler, errorHandler and phpErrorHandler keys answer as they did on Slim 3. Without a custom handler the answer is Slim 3's own page (HTML, JSON or XML by the Accept header), a path with no route still runs the app's middleware, a wrong method gets a 405 with Allow (an OPTIONS request a 200), and unsetting a handler key lets the error through to PHP, as Slim 3 did. An app served from a sub-folder keeps its base path.
  • finish() adds what Slim 3 did by itself, from the same settings: displayErrorDetails goes to the error middleware, outputBuffering to the output-buffering middleware, addContentLengthHeader to the content-length middleware, routerCacheFile to the route cache. The routing middleware runs before your own, so the route is resolved before your middleware sees the request. Body parsing is added, because Slim 3 parsed JSON and XML itself.
  • Every add() middleware keeps its ($request, $response, $next) shape through the LegacyDoublePass adapter. Move each one to PSR-15 when you next touch it, and delete the adapter when nothing uses it.
  • Slim 3 test harnesses keep working: Slim\Http\Environment becomes the generated LegacyEnvironment (with mock()), Request::createFromEnvironment() becomes LegacyHttp::createRequest(), new Response() becomes LegacyHttp::createResponse(), and $app->process($request, $response) becomes LegacyApp::process($app, $request, $response), which finishes the app once and handles the request.
  • Route groups: function () use ($app) becomes a callable that takes the group, so prefixes survive, and a route adder typed \Slim\App that a group calls is widened to take the group too.
  • $request->getAttribute('route') becomes RouteContext::fromRequest($request)->getRoute().
  • Slim 3's $request->getUri()->getBasePath(), which Slim 4's Uri lacks, becomes $request->getAttribute(\Slim\Routing\RouteContext::BASE_PATH, ''): the base path the hop's routing glue puts on every request before the app's middleware and routes run (on a Slim 3 fleet app, a signed-in /login/ answered 500).
  • Code typed with Slim 3's own Slim\Http\Request and Slim\Http\Response (the official Slim 3 skeleton's routes are) moves onto slim/http, whose decorators keep withJson(), write(), getParam() and isXhr() on Slim 4: Slim\Http\Request becomes Slim\Http\ServerRequest in use statements, fully qualified names and type hints (use Slim\Http\Request; becomes use Slim\Http\ServerRequest as Request;, so the bare name keeps working), and Slim\Http\Response keeps its name. Comments and strings are never touched. This covers src, app, routes, config, tests, public and the bootstrap file.
  • Controllers typed with Slim 3's Slim\Container get the generated LegacyContainer instead (an import keeps its bare name through an alias), and container-interop's Interop\Container\ContainerInterface, which Slim 4 no longer installs, becomes PSR-11's Psr\Container\ContainerInterface. LegacyApp::create() also takes a container the app built first.
  • When the app lists Twig-View or Twig, Twig 1 and 2's underscore class names (Twig_Environment, Twig_SimpleFilter, \Twig_Extension), which Twig 3 removed, become the namespaced classes, and new Slim\Views\Twig($path, $settings) becomes Twig-View 3's Slim\Views\Twig::create($path, $settings). The name map is Rector's own Twig set, read from the Rector Booster ships.
  • The glue is written in PHP 7.4 syntax, because the hop runs on PHP 7.4.
  • composer.json gets slim/slim ^4.15, pimple/pimple ^3 and slim/psr7 ^1.6 (the line that still installs on PHP 7.4), slim/http ^1.3 (always: the container's request and response are its decorators, so withJson(), write(), getParam() and isPost() keep working however the route is typed), plus slim/twig-view ^3.4, twig/twig ^3.8 and dflydev/fig-cookies ^3.0 when the app already lists them (fig-cookies 2 needs PHP below 8, so the PHP 8.0 hop could not install it).
  • Twig below 2.8 (1.x below 1.39) allows PHP 7.4 but trims the whitespace before every {{ there, so the PHP 7.4 hop updates it inside the app's constraints; the replay caught it on a real app.

What Booster does not do (the MANUAL list). Each run prints these as MANUAL: lines, with the file and line:

  • $settings->get('k'), now a plain array read.
  • pathFor(), urlFor() and relativePathFor() calls (build the URL with the route parser), and Twig templates that call path_for( or base_url( (Twig-View 3 has url_for).
  • getAttribute('routeInfo'), subRequest(), setArgument() calls to check, the container's router entry, and code in outer middleware that reads the route before routing ran.
  • A Slim 3 Uri base path the hop cannot place: getBasePath() on a Uri kept in a variable or property, or on a request that is not a plain variable ($this->request, the container's request), and every getBaseUrl().
  • A Twig underscore class name Rector's map does not know, and Slim\Container imported in a group use statement (import the generated LegacyContainer by hand).
  • Slim\Http\Environment imported in a group use statement (import the generated LegacyEnvironment by hand), and Slim 3's Headers, Body, RequestBody, Stream, UploadedFile and Cookies classes or new Request(...), which have no Slim 4 form: one line per file with its line numbers, the tests folder included.
  • A group callable that uses $this, or calls $app without use ($app), a route adder typed \Slim\App that was not widened, and middleware added by its container name.
  • LegacyApp::finish($app) where Booster could not place it, and a glue file that already exists and differs from the one the hop writes.

What has no hop yet#

CakePHP 3 and Slim 2 (and anything older): booster plan says Booster has no hop for them yet and keeps PHP where the framework still runs, instead of planning a break. A Slim 4 app below 4.15 is held the same way: slim-3-to-4 moves Slim 3 only, so the plan says to move Slim to 4.15 by hand. Moving a CakePHP or Slim app to Laravel is coming next; nothing in this release does it.

See also: What a hop does, The replay gate, and every hop's notes in Hops.
